newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall amid trade stalemate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall amid trade stalemate.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices turned lower early Wednesday as a stalemate developed between buyers and sellers ahead of this month's refinery turnarounds.
BP America, the main producer of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, declined to offer a price until it worked out scheduling issues.
The company last offered the local benchmark grade at $1.50 below February West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Buyers continued to bid at a $2.25 discount to WTI, and claimed BP wanted to keep the discount tight to help boost its longer-term contracts.
Buyers said they expected the next deal to close around $2 following the last trade at $1.70 under.
Chevron at Richmond, Calif, will add to the list of local refiners in shutdown when it takes three units off line in late February, a source said.
Mobil, Texaco, and Chevron at El Segundo, are also planning partialy shutdowns for maintenance this month.

Exxon, which is said to be planning maintenance at its Benecia refinery east of San Francisco during February, will bring its entire facility off line, but has already sold its ANS inventories, traders said.
"They've gotten rid of most of their crude," a trader said.
